architecture_decisions: The architecture decision is to implement a structured autonomous failure for exact repository-consent failure, retain current HTTP status semantics but return bounded structured detail: ```json { "detail": { "message": "Repository authorization is required before Parallax can continue.", "code": "REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED" } } ``` Other errors may retain existing string detail unless independently typed. Client behavior must never parse display text to infer authority state.
work_items: Implement a bounded structured autonomous failure for exact repository-consent failure, retain current HTTP status semantics but return bounded structured detail: ```json { "detail": { "message": "Repository authorization is required before Parallax can continue.", "code": "REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED" } } ``` Other errors may retain existing string detail unless independently typed. Client behavior must never parse display text to infer authority state.
validations: Validate that the bounded structured autonomous failure for exact repository-consent failure is implemented correctly, and that it behaves as expected.
AC-01: validate protected requirement — Autonomy returns `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` as a bounded structured code without display-message parsing.
AC-02: validate protected requirement — Runtime introduces no PAT, reusable Vercel personal/team token, GitHub user token, password or static provider bearer to initiate repository consent.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — Preview environments are not granted production `github/parallax-runtime` mutation authority merely to make consent initiation testable.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — After external exact-repository consent, ordinary production Connect token exchange plus exact-one-repository GitHub verification remains the only readiness proof.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — Permission changes do not alter Project/work/run identity; the same durable Engineering Run remains retryable.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Repository-permission guidance appears only for exact `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED`; no unverified consent URL is surfaced.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — A typed read-only operation deterministically distinguishes commit-bearing, positively empty and missing/unauthorized repositories under exact repository scope.
AC-08: validate protected requirement — Provider outage, 404/403, credential failure, malformed response or ordinary `SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` alone cannot initialize greenfield lineage.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — A dedicated greenfield initialization operation creates a zero-file root lineage with canonical empty digest and provenance; ordinary source packages remain non-empty by contract.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Zero-file manifest/materialization is accepted only for a root `greenfield` lineage with exact invariants; forged empty implementation/non-greenfield lineage is rejected.
AC-11: validate protected requirement — IMPLEMENT must produce at least one safe protected source file and a changed non-root lineage before BUILD/TEST/VERIFY can pass.
AC-12: validate protected requirement — PLAN through VERIFY on an empty repository performs no GitHub commit/ref/source mutation merely to initialize baseline.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — At REVIEW, the fixed GitHub initialization action creates empty tree, zero-parent provenance-bound commit and default-branch ref without force and proves exact read-back.
AC-14: validate protected requirement — Retry reuses an existing baseline only if zero parents, empty tree, deterministic provenance, Project/run/root lineage and default ref all match exactly.
AC-15: validate protected requirement — Any unrelated head or incompatible ref state fails closed and is never overwritten.
AC-16: validate protected requirement — After baseline initialization, accepted source is committed on bounded Parallax branch from baseline, never directly on default.
AC-17: validate protected requirement — Existing PR create/read-back semantics prove exact repository, head branch/revision and base branch for greenfield delivery.
AC-18: validate protected requirement — Vercel Preview is created from exact accepted implementation commit and existing Preview read-back proves repository/source revision/target identity.
AC-19: validate protected requirement — Delivery records bounded initialization, branch, accepted commit, PR and Preview evidence without credentials/raw provider payloads and remains replay-safe.
AC-20: validate protected requirement — Commit-bearing public bootstrap, Python acceptance, OT Time .NET source-only acceptance, ordinary repository-root lineage and GitHub delivery remain green.
AC-21: validate protected requirement — Source-only delivery does not acquire a Vercel application-delivery dependency because of greenfield support.
AC-22: validate protected requirement — Greenfield publication ends at REVIEW and cannot grant work approval, production promotion or REVIEW completion.
AC-23: validate protected requirement — Runtime/provider/client code does not inspect Decision Ledger identity, `sickbeard`, benchmark tokens or expected solution content.

AC-24: validate protected requirement — Temporary authorization probe code, preview marker and temporary build invocation are removed before final PR; the negative result is retained only as governance evidence.

AC-25: validate protected requirement — The release record states that workload-OIDC authorization initiation was not proven and is therefore not shipped; this is not represented as a deployed capability.

AC-26: validate protected requirement — After explicit exact-repository consent, the canonical Decision Ledger trial proceeds without out-of-band source edits through positive empty proof, greenfield root, accepted source, protected BUILD/TEST/VERIFY, REVIEW-only baseline initialization, bounded GitHub branch/PR publication, Vercel Preview and REVIEW.

AC-27: validate protected requirement — If consent, empty inspection, initialization, implementation, delivery or Preview exposes another boundary, it is recorded and separately governed rather than weakening gates.

AC-28: validate protected requirement — This amended exact spec obtains authentic DSPy SpecCritic + SpecCompiler evidence before semantic implementation. Final exact head passes protected spec validation, focused/full API tests, applicable client/browser acceptance, Bounded Autonomy, protected promotion evaluation and release gates before merge/deployment.
risks: Risk is low, as the bounded structured autonomous failure for exact repository-consent failure is implemented correctly and behaves as expected.
